  103: ## 3. PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT validation — gitleaks vs trufflehog
  109: | gitleaks | **Regex pattern + entropy** scan (pre-commit hook + git-history scan) | Fast; static patterns; catches stage-time leaks BEFORE commit |
  110: | trufflehog | **Verifier-based** with 800+ secret types + **LIVE API check** (calls AWS/GitHub/Stripe/etc. to validate detected token is actually-active) | Slower; semantic verification; eliminates false-positives |
  114: - **gitleaks**: pre-commit hook + CI gate at `git push` boundary — surfaces leaks BEFORE they reach origin
  115: - **trufflehog**: post-incident scan + git-history deep dive + GitHub-org-wide scan — catches leaks AFTER they exist, validates which are live
  118: - gitleaks = **prevention** layer (pre-commit)
  119: - trufflehog = **detection + verification** layer (post-commit, history-wide, live-validation)

   30: ## 1. License-use-class precision — trufflehog AGPL-3.0 §13
   31: 
   32: ### AGPL §13 verbatim trigger (per gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.txt)
   33: 
   34: §13 verbatim: **"Notwithstanding any other provision of this License, if you modify the Program, your modified version must prominently offer all users interacting with it remotely through a computer network (if your version supports such interaction) an opportunity to receive the Corresponding Source of your version..."**
   35: 
   36: **Trigger requires ALL of**:
   37: 1. You **modify** the Program (unmodified upstream binary use does NOT trigger §13)
   38: 2. The modified version supports **remote network interaction**
   39: 3. Users **interact remotely through a computer network**
   40: 
   41: ### Use-class analysis for claude-sota-installed runtime
   42: 
   43: | Use class | §13 trigger? |
   44: |---|---|
   45: | Local CLI binary execution (`trufflehog git file://./.` on local repo) | ❌ NO — no modification + no remote network interaction |
   46: | Library-link (importing trufflehog Go modules into proprietary code) | ❌ NO §13; would trigger §0 derivative-work clause if redistributed |
   47: | Network-served wrapper (e.g., HTTP service exposing trufflehog scan to remote users) | ✅ YES — modification + remote network interaction = source disclosure mandate |
   48: 
   49: **sss runtime usage**: CLI-binary-execution only (operator runs `trufflehog git` against local repo via Bash). NO modification. NO network service exposure. **§13 NOT triggered**.
   50: 
   51: ### Verdict
   52: 
   53: **license_precision_verdict: {trufflehog: PASS, reasoning: "AGPL §13 network-served-modification trigger NOT applicable to CLI binary execution against local repos; sss runtime is CLI-only consumer not modifier or network-server. W102 correction stands; W213 inheritance correct."}**
   54: 
   55: **Caveat**: If sss ever wraps trufflehog in a network-exposed MCP server OR modifies the source + redistributes, §13 re-triggers. Document the use-class boundary in `docs/install-provenance.md` Wave-214 install row.

  104: 
  105: ### Mechanism distinction
  106: 
  107: | Tool | Detection mechanism | Strength |
  108: |---|---|---|
  109: | gitleaks | **Regex pattern + entropy** scan (pre-commit hook + git-history scan) | Fast; static patterns; catches stage-time leaks BEFORE commit |

  111: 
  112: ### Workflow integration analysis
  113: 
  114: - **gitleaks**: pre-commit hook + CI gate at `git push` boundary — surfaces leaks BEFORE they reach origin
  115: - **trufflehog**: post-incident scan + git-history deep dive + GitHub-org-wide scan — catches leaks AFTER they exist, validates which are live
  116: 
  117: **These are complementary at sss workflow level**:
  118: - gitleaks = **prevention** layer (pre-commit)
  119: - trufflehog = **detection + verification** layer (post-commit, history-wide, live-validation)

  Podman is a daemonless, open source, Linux native tool designed to make it easy to find, run, build, share and deploy applications using Open Containers Initiative (OCI) Containers and Container Images.
  Podman provides a command line interface (CLI) familiar to anyone who has used the Docker Container Engine.
  Most users can simply alias Docker to Podman (alias docker=podman) without any problems.
  Similar to other common Container Engines (Docker, CRI-O, containerd), Podman relies on an OCI compliant Container Runtime (runc, crun, runv, etc) to interface with the operating system and create the running containers.
  This makes the running containers created by Podman nearly indistinguishable from those created by any other common container engine.

  Security
  - This release addresses CVE-2026-33414, where the podman machine init --image command when run on Windows using the Hyper-V backend can run Powershell-escaped commands from the user-specified image path on in a Powershell session on the host (GHSA-hc8w-h2mf-hp59).
  Bugfixes

  - Fixed a bug where setting a HealthCmd in a Quadlet .container file to a command that included double-quotes (") would result in a nonfunctional healthcheck due to a parsing issue (#28409).
  - Fixed a bug where FreeBSD systems could panic when inspecting containers created with the host network mode (#28289).
  API
  - Fixed a bug where the Libpod System Check endpoint could perform operations with bad data after returning a 400 error (#28350).
  - Fixed a bug where the remote attach API for containers (Libpod & Compat) could panic due to a rare race condition (#28277).
  - Fixed a bug where the Secret Create API could not create functional secrets using the shell driver due to options from the default driver being improperly added.

   15: 
   16: 12. **Upstream-install-priority over sibling-cite-import.** Every architectural primitive MUST follow source-priority order:
   17:     1. **PRIMARY (default)**: install from upstream SOTA repo via official-native-channel per cardinal-rule-6 (npm / cargo / uvx / `/plugin install` / `gh release download` / `docker pull` / `git clone` from canonical https://github.com URL with HEAD-SHA pin)

   19:     3. **TERTIARY (last-resort exception)**: cite-import-AMBER from sibling claude-sota per Section 14.5 — permitted ONLY when sota-researcher subagent invocation per cardinal-rule-10 step 4 returns **HONEST-NON-FINDING evidence** demonstrating no upstream parity exists for the primitive
   20: 
   21:     **Cite-import-AMBER is NOT DEFAULT.** Manifest rows MUST satisfy the HONEST-NON-FINDING gate predicate before STAGED → CITE-IMPORT-AMBER promotion (testable):
   22:     - (i) sota-researcher subagent dispatched with explicit upstream-parity-probe scope (probe upstream marketplaces / npm / PyPI / cargo / GitHub repos / Anthropic CC docs / ECC plugin skills / mattpocock-skills / obra-superpowers / anthropic-cookbook for primitive equivalent)
   23:     - (ii) Probe DAG (P1 LICENSE → P2 registry-existence → P3 plugin-namespace → P4 GraphQL stars-and-bands → P5 README/frontmatter → P6 deep audit) per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/agents/sota-researcher.md` returns NO install-class equivalent
   24:     - (iii) HONEST-NON-FINDING return shape per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories`
   25:     - (iv) Manifest row records HNF evidence (sota-researcher dispatch ID + probes + return) in `docs/install-provenance.md` under `effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` marker per cardinal-rule-1 cite-class lattice (sibling-derived CANNOT be elevated to TIER-1 SOTA per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8)

   31:     ### CR-12 disposition lattice (6 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series + W152-F20+ CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL codification)
   32: 
   33:     Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 6 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series mapped 5 (classes 1-5 below); W152-F20+ same-arc n=4 evidence promoted CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL as the 6th (per `codification-threshold.md` cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path):
   34: 
   35:     1. **GENUINELY-NEW** — no Anthropic/incumbent parallel exists for the primitive's scope. Disposition: **INSTALL via CR-12 PRIMARY path** (official-native-channel per CR-6). No further audit needed beyond Probe DAG.
   36: 
   37:     2. **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY** — full parallel exists in Anthropic/eee stack covering same scope and mechanism. Disposition: **REJECT-FOR-FIT** per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality without clear reason).
   38: 
   39:     3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.
   40: 
   41:     4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
   42: 
   43:     5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.
   44: 
   45:     6. **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** — Anthropic-OFFICIAL educational/reference material (cookbook notebook / official docs / non-runtime / non-install artifact) ALREADY operating as TIER-1 cite reference per existing pin in `research-protocol.md` or equivalent. Distinct from PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT (parallel runtime mechanism) and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT (core primitive new with ecosystem footprint) by requiring: (a) audited object is REFERENCE material not runtime/install artifact, (b) cite-class adoption is the CORRECT primary mode, (c) correct disposition is RATIFICATION of an existing eee rule/practice against the TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source.   117:   - npm mirror sites (e.g., `cnpm`, internal artifact servers) when `https://registry.npmjs.org` is the canonical source
